newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan army deaths in rebel raid rise to 223.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan army deaths in rebel raid rise to 223.

text.p: The Sri Lankan army's death toll rose to 223 on Monday after last week's Tamil Tiger rebel attack on a northern army base, military spokesman said.
More soldiers' bodies were recovered during clearing operations in the battle zone while some of the seriously wounded had died because of their injuries, Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said.
"The army's death toll has risen to 223," he told Reuters.

The Defence Ministry said earlier that 161 soldiers and 350 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas were killed in last Thursday's rebel raid on Paranthan, a key road junction town just south of the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The rebels said they lost 140 fighters, including 78 women, in the attack, which involved the fiercest fighting since last September.
Jayatunga denied reports in the local press that 200 soldiers were missing after the battle.
"No soldiers are reported missing," he said.
The rebels on Sunday tried to hand over through the International Committee of the Red Cross what they said were the remains of 27 soldiers killed in the Paranthan battle.
But the army refused to accept the bodies, saying they were difficult to identify, Jayatunga said.

Paranthan was the first military base to come under attack this year by the rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island.
The rebels had declared two days of mourning for their dead in the Paranthan battle, in which 20 rebel leaders died, military officials said.
Up to 700 rebels and 232 soldiers were wounded in the battle, the Defence Ministry said.
Military officials said at least eight government soldiers were also killed at the weekend, when an army tractor was blown up by a Tamil rebel landmine in the Jaffna peninsula on Sunday.
Ten soldiers were wounded in the mine explosion at Kachchai.
In another firefight in the north on Sunday, rebels killed five soldiers in a pre-dawn raid against army defences at Chettikulam in the Vavuniya district, 240 km (150 miles) north of Colombo.
